newsitem.title: USA: Oct U.S. layoffs escalate to 62 pct over Sept. [CORRECTED 15:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Oct U.S. layoffs escalate to 62 pct over Sept. [CORRECTED 15:50 GMT]

text.p: U.S. layoffs surged last month due to signs of a slowing economy, making October the highest job-cut month since January, Challenger, Gray & Christmas Inc said on Wednesday.

Announced layoffs in October totaled 47,911, up 62 percent from September's 29,632 and up 136 percent from August's 20,309. Year-to-date total of 410,208 is a 20 percent increase over 342,824 in the first 10 months of 1995, the report said.
(Corrects to read that 20 percent increase refers to year-to-date totals.)
October's total was also the highest October since 1993.
"Post-election slowdowns are not uncommon," said John Challenger, executive vice president at the international outplacement firm.

"The October job cut number is further confirmation that the economy has cooled off since the summer and that the forces driving downsizing -- technology, deregulation, cost-cutting, free-trade and reengineering -- remain undiminished," he said.
In the battle for skilled employees, many smaller firms have been losing to bigger companies with deeper pockets, the report said.
"Larger firms now have the advantage of being able to shift personnel from one area to another, and therefore retain valued employees even in this period of uncertainty," Challenger said.
The October Challenger report showed the retail sector suffered the most job cuts last month at 13,459.
The sector with the second largest job-cut total for October was insurance at 8,276, followed by automotive at 5,323, and transportation at 3,800, the report said.
